$comment: Per-template ceiling on deprecated fill-in markers, per SURFACE, enforced by
TestTemplateLegacyMarkersDoNotGrow in scripts/internal/quality. Canonical {{PLACEHOLDER}}
tokens are the target state and are not counted anywhere.
Three surfaces, because a marker can hide in any of them and measuring only the
first is what made the corpus look clean while 255 markers sat inside fenced blocks:
prose      - outside fenced blocks and inline code spans
fenced     - inside fenced code blocks. Usually a block that illustrates a format
([Module], [Number]) and usually should stay, but a fenced FORM is still a
form, and its slots were being filled by nobody.
underscore - a run of 4+ underscores used as a sign-off blank. Three or fewer is a
horizontal rule or emphasis, which is why the threshold is 4.
Re-record after a deliberate migration pass with:
go test ./internal/quality -run TestTemplateLegacyMarkersDoNotGrow -update-template-marker-baseline
Review the diff before committing: the new numbers are the record, not a target. A number
that goes UP is a template gaining legacy syntax, and deleting the entry is not the fix.
must_stay lists tokens that are permanently NOT fill-ins, one entry per file AND
surface, each carrying its reason. An entry is still COUNTED and then discounted, so an
allowance can never mask real debt in the same file and surface. Tokens are literal
substrings, not regexes; an entry that is a prefix covers its longer variants.
The test rejects a file or surface that names no measured template, and an entry with no
why, because a mistyped key discounts nothing and looks exactly like an allowance that
has already been applied - the failure reads as success.
Fenced blocks in this corpus are NOT one thing. The same file can hold docker-compose YAML
that must stay byte-identical, an ASCII wireframe that must stay a drawing, a field list
that must become tokens, and a grammar definition that must stay a pattern. Any sweep that
treats 'fenced' as a single kind will get at least one of those four wrong.

must_stay.why: Instructional prose meaning "keep writing", not a slot anyone fills.
The permitted values of a pipeline field and of a security-level field. A token that enumerates its own legal values is defining the field, not filling it.
A real YAML flow sequence in front matter: the concrete spacing scale. Converting it makes the front matter parse as a string.
The business-criticality rating scale. See ci-cd-security for why an enumeration is not a slot.
The parallel-execution flag in the format grammar, same as tasks.template.md.
Rating scales and worked threat examples. The examples illustrate what could go in a threat cell; they are not the cell.
The status flag an author marks on an unclear requirement. The trailing colon is dropped so the "...: reason" variants are covered by one entry.
Metavariable in the NFR id pattern "NFR-[Category]-XXX", not a slot.
The parallel-execution flag in the format grammar, defined literally in the file as "## Format: `[ID] [P?] Description`". Names no slot.
Rating scales and the threat/control enumeration in the control table.

Prometheus and structured-log content, not slots. {value} and [5m] are PromQL/alert templating - single-brace or bracketed by PromQL's own grammar, deliberately outside the {{ }} fill-in namespace so the linters cannot claim them. [service-name]/[version]/[uuid]/[user-id] are per-RECORD runtime values in a worked log example: no one filling in the playbook types a uuid, and the surrounding fields are already concrete, so the block is a sample of output rather than a form to complete.

YAML flow sequences in real GitHub Actions workflow files: branches:, node-version: and needs: all take a bracketed list. Converting one to {{TOKEN}} turns a valid workflow into a string or breaks the dependency graph. Same class as the front-matter spacing scale in design.template.md. Note the 25 ${{ github.* }} expressions here are NOT in this list because the curly regex cannot match '{ github.x }' - it requires a letter immediately after the brace.
The parallel-execution flag again, here inside the execution-flow fence. The agent emits it literally; it is grammar, not a slot.

The status flag the spec agent emits on an unclear requirement, inside the execution-flow fence. The prose surface already carries an allowance for the same token; this is its fenced counterpart, not a new judgement.

Type vocabulary in a worked traceability-matrix directory tree, not slots. '[module].ts' is naming a kind of file the way prose names a kind of file. Converting yields '{{CORE_MODULE_FILE}}.ts', which is neither more correct nor more fillable. The comment IDs in the same tree (FR-001, TC-003) are the same illustrative IDs used throughout the document's tables.
Fields that enumerate their own legal values. A field defining its options is not a slot - the same rationale as the prose allowances for rating scales.

ASCII wireframes and status-flow diagrams, not slots. [Logo]/[Profile] sit in a UI sketch whose every other region (Sidebar, Main Content Area, Filters) is a plain unbracketed label, so converting only the bracketed two would make one drawing speak two grammars. [Start]/[Working]/[Testing]/[Done] duplicate a row immediately above that already carries the same four stages in plain words. The three Given/When/Then metavariables illustrate the automation-test shape the surrounding prose names. A diagram is a picture of a UI; tokenising a picture is not filling it.

Foreign tool syntax that was never a fill-in. The ${...} forms are docker-compose environment interpolation - the curly regex matches their tail because it cannot see the leading '$', which is exactly the collision the {{ }} rewrite was meant to avoid. {value} is the Prometheus annotation form and [5m] a PromQL range selector. Converting any of these breaks a working config file.

The DEFINITIONS of the two most common requirement grammars in the corpus, and each is instantiated concretely inside the very same fence: 'Given [initial context/state]' is answered by 'Given a user with 4 previous failed login attempts' a few lines below, and the As a/I want/So that triple likewise. Showing a grammar instantiated is the entire purpose of stating it, so tokenising the pattern would ship a grammar definition made of tokens. It would also be wrong in kind: these recur once per acceptance criterion in every real SRS, making them per-record values rather than template fill-ins. [Use checklist from 4.5] is a cross-reference pointer, not a slot.

The TC_[Module]_[Number] test-case ID naming grammar. Eight lines earlier the same file defines the concept as {{AREA}}, so the pattern already has a canonical anchor in the corpus; rewriting the grammar itself would be a content decision rather than a marker migration.
